Alger, 9 novembre 2026 (Algeria Tech) —: Algiers, November 9, 2026 (Algeria Tech) — A major hacking campaign targeting Android and iPhone smartphone users has been brought to light by the French cybersecurity company Sekoia. Investigations reveal that cybercriminals manage to infiltrate mobile devices simply by browsing compromised web pages, without requiring any click or download from the victims.
Un mode opératoire automatisé et des log: An automated operating method and formidable spyware
Dans une enquête rendue publique le quat: In an investigation made public on November 4, 2026, the French cybersecurity company Sekoia highlighted malicious maneuvers exploiting security flaws within browsers and mobile terminal components. The attack targeting Android devices relies on a combination of vulnerabilities starting with the Chrome browser, followed by the exploitation of a Qualcomm Adreno graphics driver flaw to bypass browser protections.
Les attaquants installent ensuite un log: The attackers then install a malware dubbed "AndroSnitch", disseminated across compromised legitimate websites or fraudulent replicas of trusted platforms, such as a fake site usurping the identity of a luxury hotel located in London. This spyware proves capable of scraping Chrome cookies, login credentials, browsing history, as well as the Wi-Fi file potentially including passwords of memorized networks.
Les appareils fonctionnant sous iOS font: Devices running iOS are also subject to compromises. Flaws have made it possible to steal cookies on terminals running iOS 16 to iOS 17.4, while a vulnerability dubbed "DarkSword" allowed access to highly sensitive data on iPhones running iOS 18.5, potentially compromising messages, photographs, and saved passwords.
Implication de l'groupe APT29 et mesures: Involvement of the APT29 group and protective measures
Le rapport de Sekoia attribue cette camp: Sekoia's report attributes this cyberespionage campaign to the APT29 group, a collective of hackers associated with Russian intelligence services, whose actions primarily target individuals linked to the conflict in Ukraine, thus ruling out private individuals as primary targets despite a residual risk. The assaults rely on "n-day" vulnerabilities, corresponding to known flaws for which patches already existed, thus primarily affecting equipment lacking the latest security updates.
Face à ce péril, la parade principale ré: Faced with this peril, the main defense lies in applying security updates. Android users are notably advised to ensure their Chrome browser is updated to a version later than version 145 via the Google Play Store, and to ensure the general application of patches offered by smartphone manufacturers.
Une campagne de cyberespionnage découver: A cyberespionage campaign discovered by the French cybersecurity company Sekoia targets Android smartphones and iPhones.
L infection ne nécessite ni clic ni télé: The infection requires neither a click nor a download; a simple visit to an infected web page is enough.
Le logiciel malveillant « AndroSnitch »: The malware "AndroSnitch" steals sensitive data, cookies, history, and Wi-Fi files on Android.
La faille « DarkSword » permet l accès a: The "DarkSword" vulnerability allows access to messages, photographs, and passwords on iPhones running iOS 18.5.
Le groupe APT29, associé aux services de: The APT29 group, associated with Russian intelligence services, is suspected of being behind this campaign targeting individuals linked to the conflict in Ukraine.
